core_obligations: Write down the short exact sequence 0 to N to M to M/N to 0 for the submodule N of M (proof lines 1579-1582).
Apply localisation, which is exact, to obtain 0 to S^{-1}N to S^{-1}M to S^{-1}(M/N) to 0 (proof lines 1583-1587).
Read the last term as the quotient of S^{-1}M by S^{-1}N, giving the asserted isomorphism (proof line 1588).
proof_roadmap: Encode the quotient by an exact sequence of modules (proof lines 1579-1582).
Localise the sequence and identify the cokernel term with the quotient of the localisations (proof lines 1583-1589).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that localisation respects quotients: for a submodule N of M there is an isomorphism S^{-1}(M/N) with (S^{-1}M)/(S^{-1}N) (statement lines 1572-1576). The proof does not compare fractions by hand: it puts the quotient into the short exact sequence 0 to N to M to M/N to 0, applies exactness of localisation to get the localised sequence, and reads the quotient off the cokernel term (proof lines 1578-1589). The one substantive input is exactness of localisation, and the author spends the proof exhibiting it as a sequence rather than asserting it. H2.
